acceptanceCriteria.text: IMemoryService (src/types.ts) declares searchMany(namespace: string | undefined, queries: string[], options?: SearchOptions): Promise<MemorySearchResult[][]>, and both MemoryService and MockMemoryService implement it; the package typechecks/builds with no errors.
For a non-empty queries array, the returned array has the same length as queries, and result[i] is the result set for queries[i] (positional alignment).

For each query i, searchMany(ns, queries, opts) returns the exact same result set (same rows, same order, same distances) as search(ns, queries[i], opts) called individually — a test asserts this parity for at least one query with active SearchOptions filters.

All query embeddings are produced in a single batched embedding-provider call (this.generateEmbeddings), not one call per query — verified by a spy/mock counting provider invocations (1 call for N queries).
An empty queries array returns [] and makes zero embedding-provider calls and zero database queries.
MockMemoryService.searchMany mirrors the real service's positional/batched contract so existing consumer test patterns hold; a MockMemoryService unit test covers it.
Errors are wrapped consistently with search(): EmbeddingError propagates unchanged; a database failure surfaces as DatabaseError('searchMany').
README.md and docs/memory-service-spec.md document searchMany (API entry present) and the spec roadmap's 'Batch search operations' item is checked off; CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the feature.

explicitlyOut: Cross-namespace search or accepting multiple namespaces — that is searchAcross()'s job; searchMany is single-namespace, multi-query.
Merging, deduplicating, re-ranking, or flattening results across queries into one combined list — results stay per-query and positional.
Per-query distinct options — a single shared SearchOptions applies to all queries, matching search().
Deduplicating identical query strings before embedding.
New database schema, migrations, columns, or vector indexes.
Changes to search(), searchAcross(), or the embedding-provider interface beyond calling the existing batch method.
Streaming, pagination cursors, or concurrency/throttling controls for the batch.
0dc79a84-ae24-4aab-b08e-b43180f82d6b.killCriterion: The premise of this feature is that batching buys real efficiency over a loop of search() calls. If, once embeddings are batched, the per-query pgvector similarity searches still must run as N independent DB round-trips that cannot be combined (so searchMany is functionally just search() in a loop with no meaningful latency/cost win), stop and bring it back for a design decision — the batching abstraction may not be worth a distinct method, or may need a different shape (e.g. a single UNION/lateral-join query) than the store()/storeMany() precedent implies.

decisionsMade: Read MemoryService.ts, MockMemoryService.ts, types.ts, both test files, EmbeddingProvider.ts, and integration/setup.ts to confirm existing patterns before writing any code.

types.ts: declared searchMany(namespace, queries, options?): Promise<MemorySearchResult[][]> on IMemoryService, placed between search() and searchAcross(). No new exported types needed (MemorySearchResult/SearchOptions already exist).

MemoryService.ts: implemented searchMany after search(). Resolves namespace up-front (like storeMany), guards empty queries with `return []` BEFORE any provider/DB call, then one batched this.generateEmbeddings(queries) call, then a sequential per-query loop that inlines a byte-for-byte copy of search()'s WHERE (buildFilterConditions), decay/order expression, SELECT, maxDistance clause, LIMIT, and row mapping — guaranteeing per-query parity. Errors wrapped like search(): EmbeddingError passes through, else DatabaseError('searchMany'). Followed the codebase's duplication precedent (searchAcross already inlines search's body) rather than refactoring search().

MockMemoryService.ts: implemented searchMany by looping the existing search() (mirrors mock storeMany looping store()), which reuses all mock filter/decay/ordering logic and preserves NamespaceRequiredError behavior; empty input returns [].

Integration tests: added a searchMany() describe with 5 tests — positional length; parity vs individual search() under active filters (types/tags/minImportance/maxDistance) asserted with toEqual; single batched provider call via a spy embeddingProvider {dimensions:1536, generateEmbeddings: vi.fn} asserting toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) and called with the full queries array; empty-array returns [] with 0 provider calls AND 0 $queryRaw calls (vi.spyOn(prisma,'$queryRaw')); and NamespaceRequiredError. Imported generateMockEmbedding from setup and vi from vitest.
Mock unit tests: added a searchMany() describe with 4 tests — positional alignment vs search(), shared-filter uniformity, empty-array [], and NamespaceRequiredError.

Docs: added README searchMany entry after searchAcross (positional, single-namespace, one batched embedding call, contrast with searchAcross); added spec API entry adjacent to search(); checked off the '[x] Batch search operations' roadmap item; added a Search Latency perf note. CHANGELOG: new ## [0.6.0] - 2026-08-04 Added section. package.json: bumped 0.5.0 -> 0.6.0.

Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean, 140/140 mock unit tests pass, 76/76 integration tests pass (including the 5 new searchMany tests). Brought the project-local test Postgres up via docker compose (johnny-postgres, port 5433) with DATABASE_URL from .claude/settings.local.json, ran `prisma db push` (already in sync), ran integration suite, then `docker compose down` to restore original state.

Stop-condition check resolved to CONTINUE: batching yields a real win of N-1 fewer embedding-provider round-trips (external OpenAI HTTP calls), exactly the storeMany precedent. The per-query pgvector searches remaining as N local DB round-trips is explicitly in-scope-acceptable, so no escalation was warranted.
pathsRejected: Did NOT refactor search() to extract a shared per-query helper — out of scope, and the codebase's established pattern is inlined duplication (searchAcross already copies search's body).
Did NOT combine the N pgvector searches into a single UNION/lateral-join query — explicitly out of scope; sequential per-query DB round-trips are acceptable.
Did NOT use Promise.all/concurrency/throttling for the per-query DB searches — used a simple sequential for-loop per the plan.
Did NOT dedupe identical query strings before embedding, nor merge/re-rank/flatten results across queries — results stay per-query and positional.
Did NOT touch src/index.ts's pre-existing uncommitted CountOptions export change — it predates this task and is unrelated; left as-is.

0dc79a84-ae24-4aab-b08e-b43180f82d6b.scope:
Add a `searchMany(namespace: string | undefined, queries: string[], options?: SearchOptions): Promise<MemorySearchResult[][]>` method to the `IMemoryService` interface (src/types.ts) and implement it in both `MemoryService` (src/MemoryService.ts) and `MockMemoryService` (src/MockMemoryService.ts). Export nothing new beyond what the interface change implies.

This is the search-side mirror of the store()/storeMany() precedent: `storeMany()` takes an array, generates ALL embeddings in a single batched provider call (this.generateEmbeddings(contents)), then does the storage work. `searchMany()` takes an array of query strings, generates all query embeddings in ONE batched call, then performs one similarity search per query and returns the per-query result sets.

Shape: single namespace, many queries. Return value is `MemorySearchResult[][]` aligned POSITIONALLY with the input — result[i] is the result set for queries[i], with identical shape/ordering semantics to what search(namespace, queries[i], options) returns. The same `options` (limit, maxDistance, filters, decayOptions) apply uniformly to every query, exactly as search() interprets them. Reuse search()'s existing WHERE builder (buildFilterConditions) and ordering/decay logic so a single query through searchMany is indistinguishable from the same query through search(). Wrap errors consistently with search(): let EmbeddingError pass through, wrap DB failures as DatabaseError('searchMany'). Update README.md API section, docs/memory-service-spec.md (add the API entry and check off the "Batch search operations" roadmap item), and add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
0dc79a84-ae24-4aab-b08e-b43180f82d6b.title: searchMany() — batch semantic search over multiple queries in one call

1c32e554-4ff0-4404-a166-8ecdf3b7ceb1.scope:
What. Right now, once the counter pins at 255 the game goes quiet about it. IncomePanel keeps showing a healthy total (base gen + clicks + every memreader), HudStrip keeps showing 255, and nothing connects the two — the player has to infer from a static number that everything arriving is being discarded. The only pin affordance is MapScene.vue:396, which nudges you to inspect the core. Add a recorded discarded-income telemetry value: CounterCell.apply already computes the exact overflow when clamp_255.js caps preWriteValue (CounterCell.ts:164) — expose that per-apply amount, have SimCore accumulate it across the tick's three apply sites (click sim.ts:262, base gen sim.ts:306, extraction sim.ts:544) into a new WorldRuntime.discardedLastTick: number, reset alongside flowsLastTick/incomeLastTick, and render it as a clamped · −N row under the income panel's total plus a state on the HUD counter while pinnedAt255.

Why and how it's bounded. This is the beat kill criterion 2 rests on: the migration has to read as a threshold, not a loss, and it can only do that if the pin visibly reads as loss first — you should be able to watch a socketed memreader earn 105× the button and see all of it evaporate. Deliberately sim-side rather than a renderer derivation of income.total: rule 0.3 means the renderer displays recorded values and never re-implements clamp semantics, and discardedLastTick follows the exact precedent incomeLastTick set (plain data, per-tick reset, rides the snapshot, canonicalizes). It is telemetry only — no ⟨tune⟩ number moves, nothing behavior-shaping, so no Gate-D; the bar is that all 185 assertions stay green (0.4), the snapshot/canonical/world-snapshot shape tests get the new field, determinism stays byte-identical across restore(snapshot()), and worldless slice-0 sims are untouched. Worth noting the slice-1 human gate is still open with you — this lands before you play it, since it changes what that session is judging.

25f9c558-d84b-4e67-9bd1-960aa6e73e50.scope:
The task board's toast/sheet computes its "move to" destination list once at open, from a snapshot of task.stage. After a successful move (e.g. Implementing → Review) the task
  DOES move, but the toast keeps offering the OLD stage's destinations until closed and reopened. Fix: make the destination list a reactive derivation of the live task record in
  the store, so it updates the moment the transition streams back. The legal-move set must stay daemon-sourced (the served per-task legal moves) — the UI must not grow its own
  copy of the stage-edge table (it reflects legality, never owns it). Work is in packages/ui only. Use Node 24 via nvm (. ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 24) before any npm command. Add
  or extend a unit test covering the derivation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: FIRST BUILD STEP / residual-risk check: re-confirm the pinned answer-injection contract holds under DAEMON-IDENTICAL spawn options (allowlist + spawn-family denylist, MCP report servers, hook env, settingSources, permissionMode) - not the minimal options the orchestrator spike used. If it does not hold, STOP and raise a finding before building further.

A real agent-issued AskUserQuestion with one single-select question renders its options in VIMES (radio group, NOT Allow/Deny); selecting one option returns that option's label to the agent. Verified end-to-end by driving a real session and observing the model receive the selection - not unit tests alone.
A multi-question call mixing single- and multi-select renders all questions; each question's selection returns correctly; a multiSelect question returns all chosen labels (joined ", ").
An "Other" free-text affordance is available per question; its typed value returns to the agent as that question's answer.
Deny/decline still works: the user can decline to answer and the tool receives behavior:'deny' (or the established decline result). No regression to the deny path.
Real permission gates (Bash/Write/Edit/Read/etc.) are UNCHANGED - still Allow/Deny, behavior byte-identical to before. A permission request (no questions structure) never renders the question UI.
Dispatched/unattended sessions still auto-deny AskUserQuestion (D50) - unchanged.

New structured event + answer schemas added WITHOUT breaking existing gate_fired/gate_response consumers; the sessions projection and needsAttention still fold correctly (still surfaces attention for a pending question).
Green stays green: full scripts/ci-gate.sh passes, INCLUDING cd packages/ui && npx vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json for the .vue change. Diff read; prior assertions still green.

explicitlyOut: Permission-option variants (allow-always / allow-for-session) - separate surface
AskUserQuestion annotations / preview payloads (notes/previews) - value delivery only in this slice
Free-text-only prompts unrelated to AskUserQuestion
Any change to the real permission-gate UX beyond leaving it byte-identical
Persisting/replaying answered questions beyond the existing gate lifecycle
Multi-call / conversational question sequences beyond a single AskUserQuestion tool call
2b8c00ec-b7b6-40b5-b1dc-080cb12a8fbd.killCriterion: If the pinned answer-injection contract (return {behavior:'allow', updatedInput:{...input, answers:{[question]:string}}}) fails to deliver the selection to the model under the daemon's REAL spawn options - because permissionMode, the closed allowlist/denylist, MCP wiring, or hook env changes how AskUserQuestion resolves - STOP and raise a finding rather than shipping a second silent-empty-answer bug. Re-spike under daemon-identical options and, if the SDK offers no supported channel to inject a structured answer through canUseTool, escalate to a design decision (e.g. intercept AskUserQuestion as a client-side tool instead) before any further build.

decisionsMade: STEP 0 (residual-risk gate) FIRST: wrote scratchpad/spike-askuserquestion.mjs (isolated, drives the real @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk directly, never touches vimes.service/events.db, CLAUDE* env scrubbed) and re-confirmed the D68 answer-injection contract under DAEMON-IDENTICAL spawn. Footings 'plan' and 'default' (settingSources:['project']) both CONFIRMED: options.title is undefined for AskUserQuestion; input shape {questions:[{question,header,options:[{label,description}],multiSelect}]}; returning {behavior:'allow',updatedInput:{...input,answers:{[questionText]:string}}} delivered the selection — tool_result echoed 'TypeScript'/'Vitest, Playwright' and the model restated the picks; multiSelect value = labels joined ', ' echoed verbatim. Contract HOLDS → proceeded to build. Findings in scratchpad/spike-askuserquestion-FINDINGS.md.

The 'clamp' footing (D50 tools allowlist + spawn denylist + vimes_report mcpServer) did NOT exercise AUQ (model chose not to ask under the closed allowlist); judged MOOT/non-blocking because dispatched sessions auto-deny AUQ (D50) and the production answer path is the attended, un-clamped interactive session — exactly the two confirmed footings.

Step 1 CORE (packages/core/src/events.ts): added gateQuestionOptionSchema + gateQuestionSchema, widened gateFiredPayloadSchema with an OPTIONAL questions field (same optional-widening discipline as requestId/toolName/target — permission gates omit it, existing events/tests stay byte-identical), exported GateQuestion/GateQuestionOption inferred types.

Step 2 DAEMON CAPTURE (sessionHost.ts): restated the question shape in the daemon's zod v4 as askQuestionsSchema and BOUND it to core's GateQuestion with a two-way `satisfies` drift-guard (the documented v3-core/v4-daemon split forbids reusing core's schema object). handleGate now detects toolName==='AskUserQuestion', safeParses input.questions (fail-safe: malformed → plain gate, never throws out of canUseTool), carries parsed questions on the gateFired payload, and — since options.title is undefined for AUQ — sets prompt to the first question's text (truncated). PendingGate gained a toolName field so respondInteraction can guard answer injection.

Step 3 DAEMON RETURN (sessionHost.ts respondInteraction): added gateAnswerSchema union('allow'|'deny'|{answers:record}). On a structured answers object AND pending.toolName==='AskUserQuestion' → {behavior:'allow',updatedInput:{...pending.input,answers}} (the pinned contract). 'allow' → {behavior:'allow',updatedInput:pending.input} BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-D68 permission path. Everything else (deny, malformed, or an answers object on a non-AUQ gate) → deny. Fail-closed.

Step 4 UI: gateCard.ts — restated GateQuestion/GateQuestionOption locally (per the types.ts convention: @vimes/core is deliberately NOT a UI dependency), added a tolerant asQuestions() shape-validator, carried questions through asGateFired→deriveGateCards. GateCard.vue — renders the question surface when questions present (radio group for single-select, checkboxes for multiSelect, per-question 'Other' free-text, Submit assembling answers keyed by question text with multiSelect joined ', ', Decline emitting 'deny'; Submit disabled until every question answered) and keeps the existing Allow/Deny markup byte-identical when questions absent. StreamView.vue passes :questions and widens respond(). vimesStore.answerGate and envelope.ts ClientEnvelope widened to accept {answers}. No transport change needed — gate_response.response is z.unknown() and wsHub relays raw events.

Tests added and green: core events.test (AUQ payload validates + permission gate without questions still validates), daemon sessionHost.test (extended non-dispatched test to assert parsed questions + first-question prompt fallback; new tests for answer-injection into updatedInput, decline→deny, and the defensive guard that an answers object on a non-AUQ gate is denied), ui gateCard.test (questions carried through + malformed questions dropped to a plain card).

VERIFY-BY-BREAKING: temporarily added `|| true` to the pending.toolName==='AskUserQuestion' guard and confirmed the 'defensive guard' test reddens (answers would leak into a Bash permission gate); reverted. BYTE-LEVEL CHECK: git/grep flagged GateCard.vue as binary — caught a stray NUL byte in the OTHER_SENTINEL literal (cat -v showed ^@) and a non-existent bg-bg tailwind token; fixed both at the byte level with Python (NUL→clean ASCII sentinel, bg-bg→bg-ground). Verified 0 NUL bytes after.

GATE: npm run typecheck (tsc -b) clean; cd packages/ui && vue-tsc --noEmit clean; full scripts/ci-gate.sh PASSED (full npm test, vite build incl sw.ts, CM6 lazy-chunk check, scenario double-run byte-identical across all 7 profiles, advisories 0 high/0 crit). 2b8c00ec-b7b6-40b5-b1dc-080cb12a8fbd.scope:
Teach VIMES to handle the AskUserQuestion tool as a first-class multi-option prompt instead of collapsing every interactive request into a binary allow/deny gate. Full single-call fidelity (Wes decision B, 2026-08-04): 1-4 questions per call, each single- or multi-select, each with an "Other" free-text affordance.

BUG BEING FIXED: an agent presented multiple options via AskUserQuestion; VIMES showed only Allow/Deny, and Allow returned NO DATA to the agent (the tool ran with no selection). Root cause: AskUserQuestion arrives through the SDK canUseTool permission callback and VIMES funnels it into the same binary gate as "can I run rm?". On allow, respondInteraction returns {behavior:'allow', updatedInput: <original question>} which grants permission but injects no selected answer.

The structure dies at four typed chokepoints, all in scope to fix:
1. CAPTURE - daemon handleGate (packages/daemon/src/sessionHost.ts ~1046-1061): reads only options.title + JSON.stringify(input); never destructures questions[]/options[]/multiSelect; extractGateTarget (~493-517) has no AskUserQuestion case. Must detect toolName==='AskUserQuestion' and carry the parsed questions structure on the fired event.
2. WIRE/SCHEMA - core (packages/core/src/events.ts gateFiredPayloadSchema ~381; sessions projection ~199-221 + schemas.ts needsAttention ~15-23; ui/src/lib/gateCard.ts GateCard ~3-13): no field carries choices. Add a structured questions field to the fired event + a structured answer field to the response. Wire is already loose (gateResponseEnvelopeSchema.response is z.unknown(), wsHub.ts ~40; raw event relayed to client unvalidated) so the transport needs no change - the collapse is in the typed layers only.
3. UI - packages/ui/src/components/GateCard.vue renders only two buttons and emits only 'allow'|'deny'. Render each question with its options: radio group for single-select, checkboxes for multiSelect, plus an "Other" free-text input per question; collect selections; submit a structured answer. Keep the existing Allow/Deny path intact for REAL permission gates (a permission gate has no questions structure).
4. RETURN - daemon respondInteraction (sessionHost.ts ~856-869) + answerGate + store.answerGate (currently hard-typed 'allow'|'deny'): for AskUserQuestion, build updatedInput={...originalInput, answers:{[questionText]: value}} and return {behavior:'allow', updatedInput}. Deny path unchanged.

PINNED SDK CONTRACT (observed via orchestrator spike 2026-08-04, driving the real SDK - do NOT re-guess this, but DO re-confirm under daemon-identical spawn as the first step, see AC1):
- Input via canUseTool: { questions: [ { question, header, options:[{label,description}], multiSelect } ] }, 1-4 questions.
- options.title is UNDEFINED for AskUserQuestion - do not rely on it for the prompt text.
- Answer delivery: return { behavior:'allow', updatedInput:{ ...input, answers: { [questionText]: string } } }. The built-in tool echoes it as the tool_result and the model receives it. answers is keyed by the QUESTION TEXT; value is a STRING.
- multiSelect value = selected labels joined with ", " (our chosen encoding; the tool echoes verbatim). "Other" free-text value = the typed string.

Follows the software-orchestration discipline: deterministic/headless core, structured data only (never parse the screen), green stays green. Touches .vue and daemon/core so the gate MUST include vue-tsc and a full ci-gate; touching daemon/core means a daemon restart is required to deploy (not UI-only).

74ba0c2a-8843-4394-b41a-612fbfc5745f.scope:
What and why. Every read path in Johnny today goes through a vector query: search() and searchAcross() require a text query and an embedding API call, and get() needs an ID you already have.
  There is no way to answer "show me everything in user:123", "give me the 20 most recently updated memories of type preference", or "export this namespace" without inventing a dummy query string,
  paying for an embedding, and hoping maxDistance is loose enough. getStats() and listNamespaces() hint at an admin/inspection use case that has no corresponding way to actually see the rows. Add
  list(namespace: string | undefined, options?: ListOptions): Promise<Memory[]> to IMemoryService, implemented in both MemoryService and MockMemoryService. It returns the public Memory type (not
  MemorySearchResult) — there's no query, so there's no distance, and pretending otherwise would be a lie in the type. Keep totals out of scope: getStats().totalMemories already covers that.

  Shape. ListOptions reuses the filter vocabulary consumers already know from SearchOptions so the two feel like siblings: types?: string[], tags?: string[] (ALL-of semantics, same as search),
  minImportance?: number, plus source?: string (exact match — useful given source is the upsert key), includeExpired?: boolean (default false, matching search's implicit expiry filter), orderBy?: 
  'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'importance' | 'lastMentionedAt' (default 'createdAt'), direction?: 'asc' | 'desc' (default 'desc'), limit?: number (default 50, clamped to a MAX_LIST_LIMIT of 1000),
  and offset?: number (default 0). Offset pagination is the right call here over cursors — this is an admin/export path, not a hot loop. Two ordering details to get right: importance and
  lastMentionedAt are nullable, so decide and document NULLS LAST rather than inheriting Postgres's default (which puts NULLs first on DESC); and since ORDER BY column names cannot be
  parameterized, map orderBy/direction through an explicit allowlist to fixed sql fragments — never interpolate the caller's string into the query, even though it's typed as a union at compile
  time.

  Implementation and surface area. In MemoryService, build this as a $queryRaw with sqlJoin(conditions, ' AND '), mirroring search() at src/MemoryService.ts:210-240, and explicitly enumerate the
  returned columns — do not SELECT *, since the embedding column is Unsupported(...) in Prisma and would drag a 1536-float vector per row across the wire. Note that search() and searchAcross()
  already duplicate that filter-building block verbatim; a third copy makes the case for extracting a private buildFilterConditions(options) helper that all three call — worth doing as part of
  this change, and it's the kind of thing I'll look for in review. Wrap failures in DatabaseError('list', ...) like every other method. The MockMemoryService implementation must mirror the same
  semantics — same tag ALL-of rule, same expiry exclusion, same NULL ordering, same clamping — since the whole point of IMemoryService is that the two stay honest with each other; note that the
  mock returns memories from a Map, so an explicit sort is required for deterministic ordering, including a stable tiebreak (id) when the sort key ties. Finish by exporting ListOptions from
  src/types.ts and src/index.ts, adding unit tests to src/__tests__/MockMemoryService.test.ts (filters, ordering including the NULL cases, pagination boundaries, includeExpired, empty-namespace)
  plus an integration test asserting parity with the real service, and updating the README API Reference and CHANGELOG (a new 0.4.0 Added entry — this is additive, no schema migration).
